date_note: Date of the Digital Agency press release (公開日 20 November 2026); the agency says access took place between 30 July and 12 November and it detected it on 12 November.
exec: A Japanese government shared-services file-sharing platform may have leaked files, possibly with personal information, to unintended third parties.
plain: Japan's Digital Agency says people other than the intended recipients may have accessed files on a government file-sharing service, which may have leaked. It stopped the service on 12 November.

key_findings: The Digital Agency announced on 20 November that some files on the file-sharing service of the government-wide GSS may have leaked.
It detected on 12 November access by people other than the intended recipients and stopped the service that day; access is confirmed so far between 30 July and 12 November.
Files may contain personal information; no secondary harm confirmed so far; reported to the Personal Information Protection Commission.

summary: Japan's Digital Agency said on 20 November that some files on the file-sharing service of its Government Solutions Service (GSS) may have leaked. It detected on 12 November that people other than the intended recipients may have accessed files, and stopped the service that day; its investigation so far puts the access between 30 July and 12 November. Files may include personal information; it reports no secondary harm so far and is working with police.
title: Japan's Digital Agency says government file-sharing service may have leaked files, possible third-party access since 30 July

validation.note: Primary: the Digital Agency press release of 20 November, read in full (detection 12 November, access 30 July to 12 November, service stopped 12 November, report to the Personal Information Protection Commission, investigation with police and outside specialists, no count of files or people, no cause given). ITmedia and Cybersecurity.com (Japan) report the same announcement. The agency news list showed no follow-up notice as of 22 November.

review.note: stronger than the source: title and summary stated third-party access/confirmed access as fact; agency says files may have been accessed/leaked, period per investigation so far; added missing published date (21 Nov) for Cybersecurity.com source
